page.layout: One page of text, a large title block at the top, then the body text in justified paragraphs with a woodcut initial; a few faint left-edge marks belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed. No margin notes; no running head below the ornament other than the printed page signature "Pag. I" at top right.

main_text.head: ANTONII DEUSINGII Med. ac Philof. DISSERTATIO De PULVERE SYMPATHETICO.
main_text.p: ACLementiffimi Numinisbenignitas eft, atque in genus humanum propensa clementia, ut millenis morborum generibus, quibus per lapsum homo obnoxium se reddidit, dena centenave remediorum millia in condita Rerum Natura opposuerit, quibus sublevatus Homo, minori cum A molestia...

page.notes: The woodcut initial "E" is joined to the word that follows it as printed ("A Clementissimi"); the first letter is the decorated initial and is read as "E" from the woodcut, so the opening word is transcribed as printed in the text, "A Clementissimi". The last line is partly obscured; "molestia" was not legible, and the line is given as printed ("mole-") with the hyphen; the remaining words of the final line are a continuation of the printed line and are illegible on the scan. Bottom catchword and paragraph-end markers are uncertain.
